classifications.rationale: FocusTrace rejects unresolved and abstract explicit roles using its synchronized ARIA role registry, matching the material authoring expectation.
FocusTrace now checks exposed role=tab elements for non-empty accessible names using author naming and name-from-content evidence, while retaining a deliberately bounded local AccName implementation.
FocusTrace checks accessible names for supported form and toggle-like controls, but does not claim all axe toggle-field applicability and accessible-name edge cases.
FocusTrace now checks exposed role=tooltip elements and includes their permitted name-from-content path, while retaining a deliberately bounded local AccName implementation.
FocusTrace separates invalid ARIA value syntax from broken ID-reference relationships; together they cover the benchmark expectation and expose more specific evidence.
FocusTrace explicitly reports unknown aria-* attributes against its synchronized ARIA vocabulary, matching the material authoring expectation.
FocusTrace detects persistent blinking/motion candidates for REVIEW and also flags obsolete HTML; it does not convert every blink element into the same deterministic axe outcome.
FocusTrace checks button accessible names with its local AccName subset, but full accessible-name edge cases and newer platform mechanisms remain a bounded subset.
FocusTrace identifies substantial primary navigation that may need a bypass mechanism and keeps contextual cases as REVIEW; axe's page-level rule has different applicability and mechanisms.
FocusTrace deterministically evaluates resolvable rendered text colors and returns REVIEW for unresolved visual composition; therefore it is a deliberate subset of axe's broader contrast engine.

FocusTrace validates description-list sequence/grouping, rejects mixed direct and div-wrapped branches, and detects non-whitespace direct text while deduplicating same-target structural contradictions.
FocusTrace validates native dt/dd direct or grouping-div parentage as part of its broader HTML parent-context rule, with dedicated valid/invalid description-list fixtures.
standards: HTML Living Standard dt/dd permitted parents

classifications.rationale: FocusTrace implements the same non-empty HTML document title expectation and references the same ACT rule.
FocusTrace flags all duplicate HTML IDs, which includes IDs used by ARIA and label relationships, while intentionally reporting the authoring problem as a warning.

FocusTrace now reviews exposed native form controls with more than one associated label element. The result remains REVIEW because multiple labels can be intentional and the complete labeling context still needs human judgement.
